rhs_for_integrator: Vmax * S / (Km * (1 + I / Ki + I**2 / (Ki * Ki2)) + S * (1 + S / Ksi) + (Km * I / Ki) * (S / Kis))
sanity_expectations: At I=0 the equation reduces to substrate-inhibition Michaelis-Menten: v = Vmax*S/(Km + S*(1 + S/Ksi))
v is monotonically non-increasing in I at fixed S (more inhibitor never speeds the reaction)
At fixed I, v rises with S at low S, peaks near S* ≈ sqrt(Ksi * effective_Km), then declines (substrate inhibition)
v/Vmax stays in [0, 1] over the sampled region and never goes negative
As S -> infinity at any fixed I, v -> Vmax / (1 + S/Ksi + I/Kis) -> 0 due to substrate inhibition, NOT to a finite plateau (competitive-only kinetics would plateau at Vmax)
The uncompetitive new term (Km*I*S)/(Ki*Kis) is strongest at high S and moderate-to-high I
excitation_report: Single algebraic rate expression, RMS ≈ 0.55 (~55×sigma) over the sampled (S,I) region. The NEW uncompetitive term (Km*I*S)/(Ki*Kis) reaches a max effect of 0.0905 (~9.05×sigma) at (S≈19.5, I≈6.2), the high-S / mid-I regime where the enzyme-substrate complex population is largest and the mixed inhibitor can bind it. Passes k=5 for every term and the parent-vs-child difference.
role_corrections: S: V->V (confirmed independent axis, substrate concentration is scanned)
I: V->V (confirmed independent axis, inhibitor concentration is scanned)
Km: mislabeled input -> P (Michaelis constant; a fixed physical parameter, not a sampling axis)
Ki: mislabeled input -> P (inhibitor dissociation constant; fixed parameter, not scanned)
Kis: P->P (confirmed parameter, uncompetitive binding; value chosen inside suggested 10-1e5 range)
rationale: Structural analysis: no derivatives, no integrals, no unknown functions — a pure algebraic rate law explicitly solvable for v. Type is explicit -> evaluate_explicit. The physically scanned axes are S and I (assay design); everything else is a fixed kinetic constant. Chose Vmax=1 (arbitrary velocity unit) and Km=Ki=1 as the concentration unit, Ki2=5 (weaker second-inhibitor binding), Ksi=100 (substrate inhibition kicks in well above Km, matching the phenomenon note that Vmax is preserved), Kis=10 from the mid-low end of the suggested 10-1e5 range so the uncompetitive contribution is measurable. Ranges S in [0.1, 20] cover low, mid, and substrate-inhibited regimes; I in [0, 10] covers no-inhibitor to strongly-inhibited. 20x20 grid gives 400 points. Noise 0.01 (~1% of Vmax) makes every term (and specifically the new uncompetitive KmIS/(Ki*Kis) term at ~9×sigma) recoverable while remaining physically realistic for a plate-reader enzyme assay.
